hook.evidence: Highlights prevalence of WFL and risk of backdoor attacks in wireless settings.

gap.evidence: Notes prior surveys cover WFL or backdoors partially but not joint data/model poisoning attacks with defenses across phases.

yes_but.evidence: Acknowledges existing surveys yet stresses missing combined attack+defense treatment for WFL.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions: comprehensive attack taxonomy, phase-aligned defenses, comparisons, lessons, and future directions.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focus on data and model poisoning backdoor attacks and defenses in WFL, including metrics and comparisons.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate WFL backdoor risks; identify survey gap; present phase-based attacks; follow with phase-aligned defenses; compare performance; offer lessons and future directions.

axes: Pipeline phase (data collection, local training, aggregation)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro and related work include tables/figures to set gaps; background uses figures for WFL workflow and threat models; attack and defense sections use tables/figures per phase; comparison section uses tables; lessons/challenges are text-heavy.

figures.purpose: show survey structure and WFL threat overview

tables.purpose: compare existing surveys and highlight gap

lesson_blocks.lesson: Phase-based view clarifies where triggers/poisoning are injected and how stealth is maintained.
Phase-aligned defenses (local to post-aggregation) must balance robustness with overhead.
Using common metrics (success rate, accuracy, persistence) enables cross-method benchmarking.
Separate lessons for attacks vs defenses surface asymmetric risks and mitigation levers.
Future work should target scalable defenses, adaptive attacks, and realistic wireless constraints.

synthesis.aha_moment: Mirroring attack and defense taxonomies across WFL phases, then benchmarking with shared metrics, turns a sprawling threat landscape into parallel, comparable tracks.

methodology.selection_criteria: keywords on backdoor attacks/defenses in WFL across IEEE, ACM, AIAA, Elsevier, Springer, Taylor & Francis, Scientific, SIAM, Wiley, Hindawi

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce phase or mission, then enumerate methods with figures/tables and close with summaries or lessons.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Gap-first intro with scope and structure
steps: State the WFL backdoor risk and why wireless settings are vulnerable.
Compare prior surveys to show the missing joint attack+defense view.
List scope/contributions and provide a section roadmap.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Makes novelty explicit and orients readers before deep taxonomy.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Phase-aligned attack taxonomy
steps: Organize attacks by WFL phase (data collection, local training, aggregation).
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Phase framing mirrors the WFL pipeline and clarifies injection points.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Defense taxonomy mirroring attacks
steps: Align defenses to the same phases (local, pre-aggregation, aggregation, post-aggregation).
Include a short local-end subsection when client specifics matter.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Parallelism with attacks makes mitigation mapping straightforward.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Metrics-driven comparison then lessons/challenges
steps: Define common metrics (success rate, accuracy, persistence, overhead).
Compare attack and defense methods using these metrics.
Follow with lessons split by attacks vs defenses, then challenges/future work.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Common metrics enable fair comparisons and set up actionable lessons and research agenda.
